comparison: Strong agreement on background/contextual claims (C1-C30, C40-C42, C77-C78). Both evaluations recognize these as established knowledge from prior literature that provides necessary context. OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED citing appropriate references; peer review also marks SUPPORTED, acknowledging these foundational biological facts are not disputed.

Major disagreement on DRAM validation claims (C3-C5, C70-C74). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED through convergence of validation experiments and controls. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN due to fundamental concerns about 'editing artefacts overstating the number of actual m5C sites' and 'uncertainty regarding false positive and false negative rates.' This represents the core methodological dispute.

Disagreement on protein expression and editing validation (C31-C32, C35-C36, C43-C45). OpenEval includes these in comprehensive SUPPORTED evaluation of DRAM functionality. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, questioning whether observed editing events reflect true m5C modifications or technical artifacts, with editor noting 'uncertainty regarding false positive and false negative rates.'

Disagreement on genomic distribution and motif enrichment (C49-C55). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as part of DRAM validation. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, noting these patterns 'could reflect technical biases rather than true m5C biology' despite contrast with random controls, due to overarching false positive concerns.

Partial agreement on low-input capability (C65-C69). OpenEval includes these in comprehensive SUPPORTED evaluation. Peer review marks SUPPORTED, acknowledging these as 'technical advantages' and 'methodological improvements' that are not disputed, even while questioning overall accuracy.

Disagreement on reproducibility claims (C46-C47, shared with OpenEval R1). OpenEval finds reproducibility supports DRAM validation. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, noting that 'reproducible detection does not necessarily validate true m5C sites' given fundamental concerns about editing artifacts.

Disagreement on functional enrichment (C62) and related biological interpretation (C56-C61 in peer R6). OpenEval marks C62 SUPPORTED by standard bioinformatics approaches, noting biological significance requires further validation. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, questioning whether '>10,000 sites' represents genuine biology or 'editing artefacts,' directly undermining confidence in functional interpretations.

Both address incomplete ALYREF overlap (C48). OpenEval marks UNCERTAIN due to ambiguous interpretation (technical limitation vs. biological reality). Peer review also marks UNCERTAIN, viewing the 55.32% overlap as evidence of 'limitations in detection' within broader concerns about false positive/negative rates.

Agreement on limitations of existing methods (C13-C19). OpenEval marks these SUPPORTED as appropriately cited established knowledge. Peer review also marks SUPPORTED, extensively discussing 'short-comings of existing tools' including BS-seq artifacts and antibody method issues. Both recognize these as well-established context.

Agreement on m5C reader protein properties (C24-C27, part of C38-C39 in peer R3). OpenEval marks these SUPPORTED as established knowledge from prior work. Peer review also marks SUPPORTED, noting these foundational biochemical properties are not challenged; concerns focus on downstream application rather than underlying protein specificity.

Agreement on technical specifications (C63-C64, C75-C76). OpenEval marks these SUPPORTED as established knowledge or appropriately cited claims. Peer review also marks SUPPORTED, not disputing these specific measurements or technical parameters, including the theoretical advantage of avoiding 5-hydroxymethylation interference.

Agreement on mRNA specificity (C37). OpenEval includes this in comprehensive SUPPORTED evaluation of DRAM design. Peer review also marks SUPPORTED, noting this specificity is consistent with known biology of reader proteins and represents an acknowledged design feature rather than a flaw.

Partial overlap on reader protein mechanism (C38-C39). OpenEval includes these in comprehensive SUPPORTED evaluation of DRAM functionality. Peer review marks C38-C39 (with C24-C27) as SUPPORTED, acknowledging the biochemical basis is sound even though concerns exist about downstream application accuracy.

Partial overlap on editing specificity (C33-C34). OpenEval includes these in comprehensive SUPPORTED evaluation showing specific editing at known m5C sites. Peer review marks SUPPORTED for technical specifications, not disputing the C-to-U editing mechanism itself, though broader accuracy concerns remain.

Disagreement on BS-seq overlap interpretation (C56-C57). OpenEval includes substantial BS-seq overlap in SUPPORTED validation evidence. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, questioning whether DRAM's identification of '>10,000 sites' versus 'a couple of 100' from rigorous BS-seq represents genuine discovery or technical artifacts.
